diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus arranging the cycles of matrix $A$ into columns of $\Tilde{A}$ and applying Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) on its columns

issues.failure_explanation: Column k of W\tilde A is the DFT of the single k-th cycle, indexed by frequency. By thm:added-2, R_k(j,0) = \omega^{kj} r_{j,k}, the k-th Fourier coefficient of cycle j for each j. Hence R_k e_1 = n^{-1/2} D^k (row k of W\tilde A)^T, not D^{-k} times column k. Counterexample: A = e_0 e_0^T has only cycle 0 nonzero, so (W\tilde A)^{(k)} = 0 for k >= 1. But thm:added-2 gives R_k(0,0) = 1/n for every k. Step 4 therefore returns zero components and the sum does not reconstruct A.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Set R[k] = n^{-1/2} D^k (U_{(k)})^T, i.e. take the k-th row with phase D^{+k} and the correct FFT normalization, consistent with thm:added-2.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm 2 does not output the circulant components. Algorithm 3, which calls it to rank and build the truncated \tilde A and \tilde B, inherits wrong components.
issues.title: Circulant-decomposition algorithm extracts R_k from the wrong slice of the cycle FFT
issues.why_classification: A local index, phase and scaling correction derivable from thm:added-2 restores the algorithm and its O(n^2 log n) cost.

issues.failure_explanation: In the transformed domain, W R_t D^t B = diag(\sqrt{n} W l_t) C^t W B, as in the text's own derivation. Equivalently, the factor is the t-th cycle of WAW^*. Step 5 instead multiplies by L_A[t] = \Lambda_t, the t-th cycle of A itself. Counterexample: if all indices are selected, \tilde A = A, yet Step 5 returns W^*(\sum_t \Lambda_t C^t) W B = W^* A W B. For A = e_0 e_0^T this equals (1/n) 1 1^T B, not AB. The \Delta A \tilde B line has the same error with L_B[t].
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace L_A[t] and L_B[t] in Step 5 by the diagonal matrices of the (normalized) FFT of the first columns R_A[t] and R_B[t], i.e. the cycles of the 2D FFT.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm 3 does not compute the stated first-order approximation \tilde A B + \Delta A \tilde B.
issues.title: CD multiplication uses cycles of A instead of the Fourier eigenvalues of the circulants
issues.why_classification: A local replacement that the text already derives fixes the step without changing the method or its O(n^2 log n) cost.

issues.failure_explanation: With L = 2||D_1||_F^2||D_2||_2^2, the constant is 24L^2 = 96||D_1||_F^4||D_2||_2^4, as the proof's final display shows. The statement claims the strictly stronger exponent with 48, which the argument does not give.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 48 by 96 in the corollary statement.
issues.overall_effect: The stated tail bound is a factor of 2 too strong in the exponent.
issues.title: Corollary states a tail constant 48 but the proof yields 96
issues.why_classification: A one-constant weakening preserves the qualitative concentration result.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited theorem covers SO(n), SO^-(n), SU(n), U(n) and Sp(2n), not the disconnected group O(n). The corollary's direct application is therefore outside the hypotheses. Lemma th:expected_norm_square is also posed for unitary matrices while f is written with Q^T.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Note that f(Q) depends only on the squared entries of Q, so f(QJ) = f(Q) for a column sign flip J. Hence f has the same law under Haar on SO(n) and on O(n); apply the theorem on SO(n), or on U(n) for the complex case.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary as proved is not justified by the cited theorem.
issues.title: Concentration theorem applied on O(n), outside its listed groups
issues.why_classification: A one-line symmetry argument restores the result with the same bound.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof computes E||AB||^2/(E||A||^2 E||B||^2) = 9/16 + 7/(16n), which differs from 9/16 for every finite n. It then passes, without argument, from this ratio of expected squares to E||AB||_F expressed through the realized random norms ||A||_F and ||B||_F. That step needs concentration of all three norms, and Jensen gives only an inequality. The stated exact equality is neither proved nor true.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate as an asymptotic relation, e.g. E||AB||_F^2 = (9/16 + 7/(16n)) E||A||_F^2 E||B||_F^2. Add a concentration or variance argument for ||AB||_F, ||A||_F and ||B||_F to justify the first-moment approximation.
issues.overall_effect: The Case-2 denominator used in th:estimated_relative_error is only heuristically supported.
issues.title: Exact equality for E||AB||_F claimed; proof gives only an asymptotic ratio of second moments
issues.why_classification: It needs a limited weakening (exact to asymptotic) plus a contained concentration argument; a comparable result survives.

where $c \approx 1$ are constants for a given type of matrices.
This relative error in the product $AB$ is shown to scale only as the square of the geometric mean

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary gives only a one-sided absolute tail bound under an independent-Haar model. It does not give Var -> 0, and absolute variance is scale dependent. What is needed is relative concentration, which fails e.g. for low-rank factors, where the exponent does not grow. The residues \Delta A and \Delta B are deterministic outputs of truncated SVD, CD or FFT. Nothing establishes that they behave like independent mean-zero Gaussian matrices. The constant c is left as an unspecified per-type fudge factor.

failure_location.quote: We know that $Var[\norm{AB}_F]$ and $Var[\norm{\Delta A.\Delta B}_F]$ $\to 0$ for large $n$ and a random distribution of the entries

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict to independent Haar singular-vector models with SVD truncation and prove relative concentration under explicit spectral conditions. Otherwise present the estimate explicitly as a heuristic.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised O(n^2) a priori error estimates and the 'shown' product-of-relative-errors scaling are heuristic, especially for the CD and FFT truncations.
issues.title: A priori relative-error estimate rests on unestablished variance and residue-model premises
issues.why_classification: A rigorous version needs a contained new argument and narrows scope; a comparable heuristic estimate remains.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Now using the fact that for Haar distributed matrices we have

issues.failure_explanation: The proof uses E|Q_ij|^2|Q_kl|^2 = 1/(n(n+1)) for all (i,j) != (k,l). For Haar unitary Q this holds only when the two entries share a row or a column; for i != k and j != l it equals 1/(n^2-1). Real orthogonal moments differ again. Counterexample: D_1 = D_2 = I gives S = n deterministically, so E[S^2] = n^2 and Var = 0. The lemma gives n(n^2+1)/(n+1), e.g. 10/3 vs 4 at n = 2. lem:added-2 then gives Var = n(1-n)/(n+1) < 0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute E[S^2] with the correct Weingarten moments for the group actually used: same row, same column, and distinct row and column cases. Then redo Var(S) and the E[sqrt S] expansion.
issues.overall_effect: Both appendix lemmas and the subsequent Taylor-series formula for E||AB||_F are wrong.
issues.title: Wrong Haar fourth-moment yields false E[S^2] and a possibly negative variance
issues.why_classification: The statements are false and must be replaced by a recomputed formula; this is a contained calculation and a comparable result survives.

issues.failure_explanation: With S[i] = e^{-i/n}, all singular values lie in [e^{-1}, 1], so the spectrum is nearly flat and full rank, not low rank. About 33-46 leading components (s = 5 at n = 700) capture only about 11-15% of ||A||_F^2, giving truncation relative error of about 0.92-0.94. Under the paper's Haar model the zeroth-order product error is about 0.98. A 5% error at s = 5, as reported, is impossible under the stated construction.

failure_location.quote: S[i]=$e^{\frac{-i}{n}}$, and S[i]=$\frac{n-i}{n}$ for $i=0,1,2,\dots,(n-1)$ were used for generating Type-1 and Type-3 matrices respectively.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the singular-value profile actually used for Type-1 (a genuinely fast-decaying or low-rank spectrum), consistent with the reported results.
issues.overall_effect: The Type-1 experiments are not reproducible from the stated construction, and their description as low rank is false.
issues.title: Stated Type-1 generator is full rank, contradicting 'low-rank' and the reported results
issues.why_classification: Correcting the generator description is local and affects no formal result.
